title: Wickens beats di Resta by 0.362s to win Nürburgring Race 2
dek: Robert Wickens won Race 2 at the Nürburgring for Mercedes-AMG by 0.362 seconds from di Resta after an early pit stop, while Auer's lap-six spin let Ekström extend his title lead to nine points.

chapters.title: Mercedes on a high, Ekström under pressure
text: Saturday had belonged to Mercedes. Lucas Auer won Race 1 from pole in changing weather as the manufacturer took the first four places, while Mattias Ekström gambled on slick tyres just as rain returned and finished 15th without points. The title picture tightened to 128 points for Ekström, 127 for Auer and 124 for René Rast, with Rast carrying a five-place grid penalty into Sunday after his third warning of the season.

Sunday's race was the 14th of 18, with four races to follow after it. With the Audis again running the heaviest cars on the grid, the question was whether Auer could take the points lead on a dry track.

chapters.title: Wittmann snatches pole from di Resta
text: Sunday's qualifying was dry, in contrast to the day before, and the lap times were around five seconds quicker. The drivers needed a couple of laps to bring their tyres up to temperature, and after the first runs BMW held the top two places on the timing screens. Tom Blomqvist went top with a minute left, only for Marco Wittmann to take over.

Paul di Resta then crossed the line with 1:21.052 and looked to have taken pole for Mercedes-AMG, but Wittmann improved to 1:20.936 on the final lap to start from the front, 0.116 seconds clear. Robert Wickens was third on 1:21.121 and Auer fourth on 1:21.128, with Blomqvist, a mere 0.007 seconds slower, fifth. Timo Glock and Augusto Farfus were sixth and seventh, and Gary Paffett, Bruno Spengler and Edoardo Mortara completed the top ten.

Audi had another bad session. Jamie Green was the best of the Audi RS 5s in 11th, championship leader Ekström qualified 14th and Rast 13th; Rast's grid penalty dropped him to 18th and last, which moved Ekström up to 13th on the grid.

chapters.title: Di Resta leads, Auer spins
text: Di Resta made the best start and led into Turn 1 from Wittmann, with Auer third and Wickens fourth. Rast and Mike Rockenfeller both stopped at the end of the first lap, and Rast lost further time with a slow stop.

Di Resta pulled out a gap of a couple of seconds, but on lap six Auer took too much kerb at Turn 4 and spun from third place. He dropped to 13th, and the mistake effectively ended his chance of taking the championship lead. Wittmann gradually reeled in di Resta and passed him with a dive down the inside at Turn 1 on lap 15.

chapters.title: Wickens undercuts the leaders
text: Wickens stopped a few laps before the leading pair, on around lap 13, and the decision decided the race. Wittmann and di Resta came in together on lap 16 or 17, di Resta losing time with a problem at his stop, and Wickens came out in front of both after passing several cars on fresh tyres, including Farfus and Wittmann.

Spengler, Ekström, Green, Nico Müller and Loïc Duval waited much longer. Ekström and Green ran well on long first stints and Green was the last man in, on lap 30. Around lap 27 Glock ran into the back of Müller's Audi at the chicane, and Müller, with heavy damage, did not finish the race. Wittmann lunged at Wickens at Turn 1 at around two-thirds distance, the pair touched and Wickens kept the place.

chapters.title: Wickens holds on by 0.362 seconds
text: Wittmann struggled with graining on his front tyres after the contact, and with six laps remaining di Resta drafted past him for second. The Scot, who was about four seconds behind Wickens, closed the gap lap by lap and was right on his gearbox as they started the final lap, but Wickens held on to win by 0.362 seconds in 56:49.795.

Wittmann finished third, 7.589 seconds behind, with Spengler 7.955 seconds off the winner in fourth and Maro Engel fifth. Ekström was sixth from 13th on the grid, and he and Green swapped places in the closing laps after Ekström made light contact with Farfus before re-passing Green on the penultimate lap. Glock was eighth, Farfus ninth and Blomqvist tenth. On the final lap Maxime Martin and Paffett touched at the chicane and the Mercedes spun, finishing 14th, with Martin 11th.

chapters.title: A double for Mercedes, a gift for Ekström
text: Wickens took the sixth DTM victory of his career and gave Mercedes-AMG a clean sweep of the weekend, after Auer's win on Saturday. He called it a crazy race and said the stop had been decisive, adding that he had been lucky the race had not been a lap longer because di Resta was pushing hard. He also reported steering damage after the contact with Wittmann at Turn 1. Di Resta, who struggled to get heat into his tyres in the cold, said he had been able to recover to second after a good second stint.

Wittmann was not unhappy with third place from pole, given the damage to his front end and the graining that followed. BMW management said the team had left too many points on the table over the weekend and described the racing as hard, at times overly hard. Wittmann climbed to fourth in the standings, behind Rast. Spengler, Glock, Farfus and Blomqvist all scored for BMW in the race.

The result of the day was Auer's lap-six spin. He had come to Sunday one point behind Ekström and with a good chance of taking the lead, but finished 13th. He apologised to the team, saying he took full responsibility, while Mercedes DTM boss Ulrich Fritz called the opportunity a gift the team had not used, though he added that four races remained. Ekström, with a long first stint and a late stop, repaired the damage with sixth and extended his lead to 136 points, nine ahead of Auer and 12 ahead of Rast on 124. Only he and Green scored for Audi.

Rast had a difficult day, starting last and finishing 12th after a slow stop, while Müller's Audi was left with heavy damage after the contact with Glock. The championship moves to the Red Bull Ring in Austria for the next round, with four races to go.

facts.v: Wickens won Race 2 in 56:49.795 over 40 laps, 0.362 seconds ahead of di Resta, with pole-sitter Wittmann third.
